inspected_contracts: JavascriptPolyfill owns independent scheduled timers and cancels them on teardown
HistoryController owns application history independently of plugin sessions and saves selection removal as a batch
reference.inspection: Architectural and lifecycle facts only; independent Rust implementation

review_findings.problem: A nonempty plugin command queue always won over expired timer deadlines.
review_findings.resolution: Ready commands and timers alternate without delaying cancellation.
review_findings.before_fix: The first regression failed: the timer ran after all eight queued events rather than after the first event.

review_findings.problem: Playback notifications acquired recent media then history, while history actions held history before acquiring recent media. Concurrent paths could deadlock.
review_findings.resolution: History observations return owned entries before recent media is locked. History actions release their guard before publishing snapshots. Clearing holds history across the disk and memory changes, preventing concurrent observations from restoring cleared rows.

review_findings.problem: Removing a selection cloned and saved the full archive once per row, with partial deletion possible if a later save failed. Clear-history success could also overwrite a plugin refresh error.
review_findings.resolution: Remove all selected rows in one persisted change, mutate memory only after success, and retain refresh failures in the UI status.

review_findings.problem: Text/download writes checked existence separately from truncating writes. Text reads trusted metadata size before an unbounded read.
review_findings.resolution: One shared writer uses exclusive file creation outside private plugin storage. Reads verify regular-file metadata from the open handle and enforce the byte limit during reading.
review_findings.scope: Exclusive final-file creation and bounded reads; no claim of eliminating all path-resolution races or providing complete filesystem sandboxing.
